question: With four photos per feature, does weighting a person's vote by their score beat a plain majority? UPDATE_22 section 1 answer 1; the planner's method from UPDATE_09 item 4

summary.statement: In groups of 5, plain majority is best in 3 of 5 skill patterns. Feature only weights clearly lose to plain majority in 5 of 5, by 12.1 to 20.6 points. A weighted method clearly beats plain majority in 1 of 5 (third_at_chance), by at most 1.1 points (shrunk_k6). Passers only clearly beats plain majority in 2 of 5 (uniform_per_person, third_at_chance), by at most 2.2 points.
summary.beats_rule: a method clearly beats (or loses to) plain majority when its mean share right is higher (or lower) by more than twice the Monte Carlo standard error of the paired difference

parameters.answers: yes or no only, so each vote is right or wrong; Can't tell is not modelled

patterns.equal: skill 0.70 for every person and feature
patterns.normal_per_person: one draw per person from normal(0.70, sd 0.07), used for all four features
patterns.uniform_per_person_and_feature: one draw per person and feature from uniform(0.50, 0.95)
patterns.uniform_per_person: one draw per person from uniform(0.50, 0.95), used for all features
patterns.third_at_chance: exactly 13 of 40 people (40 / 3 rounded to the nearest whole person) at 0.50 on every feature; the rest one draw per person from normal(0.80, sd 0.06), used for all four features

parameters.at_chance_rounding: 40 / 3 = 13.33, rounded to the nearest whole person
parameters.halves: for every feature 2 of its 4 items go to half A and 2 to half B; score on one half, vote on the other, then swap; results are over both ways
parameters.paired: every method is scored on the same populations, splits and groups

methods.passers_only: people with C >= 6 vote by plain majority; when nobody in the group passed or the passers tie, the whole group votes by plain majority

symbols.c: right of the 2 calibration items of the voted item's feature

parameters.vote_rule: sum of w over people right minus sum of w over people wrong; above zero is right
parameters.tie_rule: a sum of exactly zero (a tie, including every weight zero) counts as wrong for every method; sums within the tie tolerance of zero are treated as zero to absorb floating point rounding
parameters.monte_carlo_error: standard error across the simulated populations: the standard deviation of the per population mean share right over the square root of the number of populations
